posts.card_claim: Rude happened. Harmed is a story you can decline.
posts.card_cite: Moodius · after Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 2.1 and 4.7
posts.text:
Marcus Aurelius started his mornings expecting difficult people (Meditations 2.1). Not to turn cold. To stop being surprised.

Then Meditations 4.7: drop the judgement "I've been harmed", and the harm goes with it.

Rude happened. Harmed is a story you can decline.

Who are you getting ready for today? The role, not the name.

Asking for help is a skill, not a confession.

Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 7.7 (Long): "Be not ashamed to be helped."

Who's one person you could ask this week, and what's stopping you?

posts.card_claim: The argument took five minutes. The replay takes three hours.
posts.card_cite: Moodius · after Seneca, Letters 13.4 and Epictetus, Enchiridion 5
posts.text:
The argument took five minutes. The replay takes three hours.

Seneca saw it (Letters 13.4): we suffer more in imagination than in reality. Epictetus named the cause (Enchiridion 5): it isn't what happened, it's the judgement about it.

Tonight, write the judgement down in one sentence. Then ask: is it true, and is it useful?

What's the argument you've replayed most this year?

Asked whether he'd rather do wrong or suffer it, Socrates said: "If I must choose between them, I would rather suffer than do." (Plato, Gorgias 469c, Jowett)

Whoever cheated you has to live with a cheat. You don't.

Have you ever been glad, later, that you didn't get even?

posts.card_claim: End the day with a review, not a trial.
posts.text:
The 5-minute evening review the Stoics actually ran.

Seneca describes it in On Anger 3.36: lights out, the day replayed in order, three questions, nothing hidden. In paraphrase: what bad habit did I cure today, what fault did I resist, in what way am I better?

Not a trial. A review. Phone in another room, one notebook.

Which of the three is hardest for you?

You didn't choose your family, your city or your century. Neither did Marcus Aurelius.

Meditations 6.39 (Long): "the men among whom you have received your portion, love them, but do it truly, sincerely."

Who's someone you were given rather than chose, and what's one good thing about them?

posts.card_quote: Look within. Within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up, if you will ever dig.
posts.card_cite: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 7.59 · tr. George Long
posts.text:
The person you want to become isn't in a course, a new city or someone else's approval.

Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 7.59 (Long): "Look within. Within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up, if you will ever dig."

What's one good thing in you that you've been underusing?

A hard season isn't proof you're doing life wrong. Sometimes it's just the season.

What's helping you get through this one?

— Moodius

posts.card_claim: You're not lazy. You're avoiding a feeling.
posts.text:
You're not lazy. You're avoiding a feeling.

Psychologists link a lot of procrastination to mood repair: you put the task off to escape how it makes you feel. Doubt, boredom, fear of doing it badly.

Marcus caught himself too. Meditations 2.4 (Long): "Remember how long you have been putting off these things."

Name the feeling. Shrink the start to two minutes. Bring the feeling with you.

What's the feeling behind the thing you're putting off?

Likes are a vote from people who gave your post half a second. Your own opinion of you has watched every day of your life.

What would you post if nobody could see the likes?

— Moodius

posts.card_claim: Rehearsing a disaster isn't preparing for it. It's living it twice.
posts.text:
Your mind runs the worst case on repeat because rehearsing feels like preparing. It isn't. It's living the bad day in advance, often more than once.

Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 7.8 (Long): you will meet future things "having with you the same reason which now you use for present things."

Ask for the next action. If there isn't one, come back to the room.

What does your mind rehearse most?

Solitude you choose recharges you. Loneliness drains you.

If you can't tell which one this is, ask: would I pick up if someone called?

— Moodius

posts.card_quote: The greatest part of what we say and do being unnecessary, if a man takes this away, he will have more leisure and less uneasiness.
posts.card_cite: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 4.24 · tr. George Long
posts.text:
Burnout often isn't too much work. It's too much unnecessary work.

Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 4.24 (Long): "The greatest part of what we say and do being unnecessary, if a man takes this away, he will have more leisure and less uneasiness."

One question for every task today: is this necessary?

What could you drop this week that nobody would notice?

Gregor Samsa wakes up as an insect, and his first real panic is that he's late for work.

If the job is the first thing you think of when you're ill or falling apart, it has more of you than it paid for.

What would you stop doing if work didn't count tomorrow?

— Moodius, on Kafka's The Metamorphosis

posts.card_claim: The comment took ten seconds. The story you add to it takes the day.
posts.text:
Ninety-nine kind comments, one sharp one, and you replay the sharp one. Psychologists call it negativity bias.

Epictetus, Enchiridion 20 (Higginson): "It is your own opinion which provokes you."

The comment took ten seconds. The story you add to it takes the day.

Buy time. Don't reply today.

Do you react or respond more often? Be honest.

The early version of a better life looks a bit ridiculous from the outside. You leave at eleven. You don't drink. You carry a book.

What's the habit you'd start if nobody could see?

— Moodius

posts.card_claim: Pick friends you'd be glad to become.
posts.card_cite: Moodius · after Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics IX.4 and IX.12
posts.text:
The myth: you are who you are, whoever you're around.

Aristotle disagreed. Nicomachean Ethics IX.12 (Ross): friends "take the mould of the characteristics they approve" from each other. And IX.4: "his friend is another self."

Pick friends you'd be glad to become.

Who's one person who made you better just by being around them?

If anger was the only feeling that was safe to show growing up, it ends up carrying everything else: the hurt, the shame, the fear.

What's usually under yours?

— Moodius

posts.card_claim: Stop explaining your philosophy. Show it.
posts.text:
Epictetus, Enchiridion 46: sheep don't throw up their grass to show the shepherd how much they've eaten. They digest it, and produce wool and milk.

Stop explaining your philosophy. Show it.

One question for tonight: where did what you believe actually show up today?

There's a version of independence that's really just fear with good posture. You don't reach out, so you can't be turned down.

Who have you been waiting on to message first?

— Moodius

posts.card_claim: The wild horse isn't the enemy. It's energy.
posts.text:
Plato, Phaedrus 246b (Jowett): the soul as a charioteer with two horses, "one of them is noble and of noble breed, and the other is ignoble."

The wild horse isn't the enemy. It's energy. You don't get rid of it, you train it: notice the pull, name what it wants, give the energy a job.

Which horse wins more often in your week, and when?

In a 2014 study (Wilson et al., Science), many people left alone with their thoughts for 15 minutes chose a mild electric shock over sitting there.

The urge to grab the phone isn't weakness. It's what quiet feels like when you're out of practice.

Five minutes tonight, nothing in your hands. How long did you last?
